MONGRAIN / TECHNICAL RESEARCH · OCTOBER 8, 2026

14 wall systems.
Documented layers and junctions.

A source-linked analysis of SOPREMA’s wall catalog, with extracted technical drawings and a precise correction plan for the envelope animation. Research reference, not for construction or a verified test listing.

Findings14 systemsLayer orderTechnical propertiesJunction drawingsViewer changesLimitsPreviewsPDF index

The viewer needs assembly-specific geometry

The catalog contains 14 systems, not 14 interchangeable versions of one ten-layer wall. They resolve into protected exterior walls, protected hybrid walls, unprotected ALU walls, hybrid PLUS/cellulose walls, XPS walls, SPF walls and interior acoustic partitions. Substrate and attachment differences still need separate selections within these families.

The current animation is a useful conceptual envelope viewer. Its wall data in mongrain-envelope-refined.html has ten generic entries, including separate air/vapour planes, one continuous-insulation slab, block-like clips and a flashing entry. These should become documented system objects with localized details, rather than a universal stack. No animation code was changed during this research.

Scope, retrieval and document provenance

Coverage: all 14 wall systems loaded from the specified catalog, including both SPF systems behind pagination; 13 distinct product/component pages; 74 unique product-document links inventoried. Downloaded and parsed 96 public PDF records (296 pages): 66 detail records, 8 guides, 12 technical data sheets and 10 brochures. Two record pairs are byte-identical: the cellulose acoustic guide/brochure and two SOP300-10 listings. The package therefore stores 94 distinct original PDFs, including 65 distinct standalone detail PDFs.

Drawing discovery used product-document overlays plus paginated documentation searches for SOPRASEAL and SOP300, with Walls/Details filters. The SOP300-filtered search returned 114 file records (58 PDFs and 56 CAD links); additional SOPRASEAL results supplied VP and foundation-transition details. This is complete catalog-system coverage, not a claim to have captured every PDF anywhere in SOPREMA’s website.

All downloaded PDFs were text-extracted and checked for page counts. The standalone detail pages and selected guide drawings were also rendered and visually reviewed. Text extraction alone misses image-based acoustic details; those pages were rendered separately. PDF page references here are one-based physical PDF pages.

The 74-link component index retains SDS, EPD and other links that were not included in this drawing-focused download. No SDS or environmental certification is treated as a construction drawing. The scope is walls and their roof/foundation interfaces; it is not a full review of the separate roofing or foundation catalogs.

Protected systems additionally list mineral wool and ACS clips. Component tables are not installation-order diagrams. Some source role labels are clearly inconsistent with the actual product documents: ACS is called “Adhesive Mortar” on the concrete/XPS and steel/SPF pages; PLUS is called “Armed Adhesive Mortar” on the wood hybrid page. The wood hybrid also repeats cellulose under insulation and soundproofing. These are catalog-label issues, not additional adhesive layers or a second cellulose cavity. The mapping retains each official system URL and uses the technical documents to interpret the physical products.

Inside-to-outside reading of the assemblies

These are schematic interpretations for animation, not installation instructions or exact tested assembly specifications. Clips, fasteners and flashing are localized/penetrating elements, not uninterrupted planes. The retention membrane may have vapour-control properties depending on the selected product; do not always draw retention and vapour control as two distinct films.

FamilySchematic reading
protected-exteriorInterior finish / backup as designed → CMU or steel framing + sheathing → Primer where required → STICK 1100 T: one combined air/vapour membrane → SOPRA-ISO V ALU → Outer mineral-wool protection → Project-designed cladding support through insulation → Drained air space → Cladding
protected-hybridInterior finish / service furring as detailed → Interior vapour control + cellulose retention details → Wood or steel studs with cavity cellulose → Exterior sheathing → STICK VP: vapour-permeable air barrier → SOPRA-ISO V PLUS → Outer mineral-wool protection → Project-designed cladding support → Drained air space → Cladding
exterior-aluInterior finish → Uninsulated steel framing + sheathing OR concrete backup → Compatible primer → STICK 1100 T: combined air/vapour membrane → SOPRA-ISO V ALU → Project-designed support (ACS where listed) → Drained air space → Cladding
hybrid-plusInterior finish / service furring as detailed → Interior vapour control + cellulose retention details → Wood or steel studs with cavity cellulose → Exterior sheathing → STICK VP: vapour-permeable air barrier → SOPRA-ISO V PLUS → Project-designed support → Drained air space → Cladding
exterior-xpsInterior finish → Uninsulated steel framing + sheathing OR concrete backup → Compatible primer → STICK 1100 T: combined air/vapour membrane → SOPRA-XPS 20 → Project-designed support (ACS where listed) → Drained air space → Cladding
exterior-spfInterior finish → Uninsulated steel framing + sheathing OR concrete backup → Compatible primer → STICK 1100 T: combined air/vapour membrane → Local mechanically-fastened membrane retention bars → SOPRA-SPF 200, sprayed in permitted lifts → Project-designed support (ACS where listed) → Drained air space → Cladding
interior-acousticGypsum face / layers per selected acoustic configuration → Optional resilient channels as detailed → Stud framing with cavity cellulose → Retention membrane / strips / patched fill openings → Other gypsum face / layers per selected configuration

For protected systems, the ACS guide p12 explicitly installs polyiso before outer stone wool. The 2023 protected-assembly article describes a two-inch mineral-wool strategy; that is an article example, not a universally verified minimum thickness. No exact S134 test listing/report was retrieved to establish approved wool density, insulation thickness, clip spacing, cladding or substrate combinations. The model should show “schematic thickness / confirm tested configuration,” rather than silently defaulting to a claimed approved stack.

For concrete-labeled catalog systems, several available drawings are explicitly masonry/CMU. They are useful product-family references but do not establish exact cast-in-place concrete attachment or transition details. The report labels those mismatches rather than presenting the closest drawing as an exact match.

Technical properties that change the model

The figures below come from the retrieved technical sheets. They are product properties, not whole-wall effective R-values or guaranteed field performance. ASTM E96 dry/wet-cup values are not interchangeable. LTTR and 90-day-aged thermal values also use different bases. Preserve the method, thickness and document revision whenever displaying a performance figure.

Product / sourcePhysical and performance factsInstallation constraints / limitsAnimation interpretation
STICK 1100 T
TDS - SOPRASEAL STICK 1100 T
Revision code: 260325SCANE		1.0 mm / 40 mil self-adhered SBS-modified bitumen with woven tri-laminated polyethylene facer. Combined air/vapour barrier; water-vapour permeance <0.04 perm (ASTM E96 A/B).Compatible primer required; clean, sound, dry substrate. General overlaps ≥50 mm; roll membrane. Winter grade application −10 to 10 °C; summer 10 to 50 °C; UV exposure up to 90 days. Local details may specify larger overlaps.A single thin membrane on sheathing/backup; darker sheet with printed facer, lapped seams and localized turned transitions. SPF-over-membrane restraint must be included.
STICK VP
TDS - SOPRASEAL STICK VP
Revision code: 260408SCANE		0.6 mm / 24 mil tri-laminate polypropylene membrane. Vapour-permeable air barrier: 11 perm dry-cup (ASTM E96 A), 14 perm wet-cup (E96 B).Primer-free on most substrates; VP primer may be required for particular conditions. Longitudinal overlaps ≥50 mm; transverse ≥75 mm. Application −7 to 40 °C; UV exposure up to 180 days.Light/printed fibrous membrane, not a vapour-barrier label. Keep localized 1100 T transitions separate from the field VP membrane.

Do not turn the patch into a continuous wall layer.

SOPRASEAL STICK 1100 TC: this is the thirteenth linked catalog component and is listed for membrane transitions. Its product overlay supplied SDS links, but no separate technical data sheet was retrieved. Do not claim a verified TC-specific thickness, roll width, permeance or interchangeability from the 1100 T TDS alone. The drawings that explicitly say 1100 T cut/pre-cut rolls are cited as such.

This research is not an installer training program. Surface preparation, compatible accessories, weather limits, safety, application equipment, certification and project specifications still govern the work. In the viewer, label an installation playback as “illustrative sequence; consult current guide” and provide its source link.

w-structOne generic backup shapeSwitch between hollow-CMU masonry, concrete and metal/wood stud framing. Cavity fill should not cover studs.System substrate + relevant base-wall drawings
w-sheathOne sheathing planeKeep sheathing for framed walls; do not imply it is required over every masonry/concrete backup.SOP300-17 vs SOP300-18
w-air / w-vapTwo generic control-layer entriesCombine these into one 1100 T product plane for exterior-only systems; use VP outside and depicted vapour control inside for hybrids.1100 T / VP TDS; SOP310-01/02
w-ciOne insulation slabChoose ALU foil-faced, PLUS matte-faced, XPS grey, or irregular SPF. Add a distinct mineral-wool layer for protected variants.Insulation TDS; ACS guide p12
New: cavity infillNo cellulose-specific physical cavityFill individual stud bays and show retention/patch details, rather than adding cellulose as a flat exterior plane.Cellulose guide p16
w-clipBlock-like clip depictionUse real Z-shaped / nested-L geometry, back pad, screw paths and the supporting girt. Keep anchorage attached to backup in exploded mode.ACS guide pp5/13; structural guide p15
w-cavLayer-like rain-screen volumeRepresent as empty air space with a dimension/ghost boundary, not a solid building product.Catalog-related detail sections
w-girt / w-cladGeneric rail and claddingCladding-specific support: brick ties are not panel girts. Never display brick anchors, wood strapping and ACS rails as one mandatory universal stack.SOP300-17, SOP310-02, ACS guide
w-flashGeneric flashing entryUse local wall-base, sill, jamb, parapet, movement-joint and penetration pieces with continuity to the field membrane.SOP403 / 303 / 302 / 306 / 307 families
Roof / foundation scopeGeneric envelope layersRetain as contextual interfaces only until their separate system catalogs are researched. Show XPS 30 and drainage orientation when the actual SOP403 detail calls them out.SOP403-07 through -10

Recommended UX: select a named system first, then choose an assembly view or a junction detail. Offer three distinct modes: assembled section, exploded explanation and illustrative installation sequence. Keep one selected material highlighted, with its product sheet and applicable drawing beside it. In exploded mode, use connector lines back to the assembled positions; do not visually imply that anchors float between disconnected parts.

Show true membrane/board thickness values only when documented, but exaggerate thin membranes for readability with an explicit “visual thickness exaggerated” label. Use a cutaway to reveal cellulose/steel stud cavities, and use a transparent outline for empty air space. Keyboard-accessible system selection, descriptive button labels, a reduced-motion option and a pause control should be part of the next implementation.

The included animation-system-mapping.json is a proposed data contract with all 14 source URLs, material families, schematic layer readings and applicability limitations. It contains null rather than invented tested thicknesses. It does not modify the animation or automatically generate verified three-dimensional/CAD geometry.

What is not verified, and what must be checked before construction

  • Exact protected-wall fire-test configuration: the catalog and article state CAN/ULC-S134 results, but the complete applicable listing/test report was not obtained. No arbitrary cladding, insulation thickness, mineral-wool density or substrate is declared compliant here. S101 fire-resistance information in an SPF brochure is a different test basis and is not an S134 substitute.
  • Build Better guide: its public download path redirects to a form requesting contact/business information and marketing consent. No form was submitted. The full guide and its effective-R/thermal-bridge tables are not in this package. Form-gated guide
  • Structural spacing: ACS charts depend on substrate, screw capacity, cladding weight, wind and assembly depth. The structural guide pp3–4 requires project-specific engineering review. No clip grid was engineered for Mongrain.
  • Hygrothermal design: a vapour-permeable exterior membrane does not, on its own, establish the correct interior vapour control or safe insulation ratio for a climate/building. Do not claim condensation-safe assemblies without the applicable design/analysis.
  • Exact concrete counterparts: some retrieved sheets show CMU/masonry instead of cast-in-place concrete. The matrix flags those related references. Do not relabel their structural attachment as an exact match.
  • 1100 TC: a separate TDS was not retrieved; SDS links are not a substitute for dimensions and performance verification.
  • Scale / quantities: N.T.S. and N/A sheets must not be measured to generate construction dimensions, clip quantities or fabrication files. Use stated dimensions and project drawings.
  • Current revisions: source links may update. Retained PDFs and their SHA-256 hashes define this snapshot. Where guide illustrations are older, current product sheets and project/manufacturer guidance must resolve conflicts.

All original technical drawings remain the work of their stated publishers. This extraction preserves source credit and copyright; it does not grant new publication, modification or redistribution rights. Confirm the rights before placing manufacturer drawings in a public-facing Mongrain website.

Full-resolution PNGs are in drawing-previews/. The companion PDF retains vector source pages and provides a clickable source index. These previews are for orientation; inspect the original PDF and its complete notes before using a detail.
